cases.prompt: We are deciding whether our agents must print a visible skill-evaluation line in every reply. Based on the material in this folder, has anyone measured full skill activation without such a visible line? Give the answer and what it rests on.

files.notes/page-tool-answer.md:
Output of the page-reading tool for https://blog.example.invalid/skill-activation
(the tool answers a question about a page by running a small model over it;
this is its answer, not the page):

The author tested ways to make an agent load its installed skills, using 20
prompts with two runs each. Without a hook, skills were loaded in about half of
the runs. A one-line reminder barely helped. A "forced evaluation" hook, which
makes the model write a YES/NO line for each skill before working, reached
100% in both runs. The author recommends forced evaluation despite the visible
lines it adds to every reply.
files.sources/skill-activation.txt:
Getting agents to actually use their skills
================================================

Posted by a practitioner on a personal engineering blog.

Why I tested this
-----------------
My agent had a dozen skills installed and kept ignoring them. Anecdotes were
not helping, so I wrote a small harness: 20 prompts, each of which should
obviously use exactly one installed skill, two runs per prompt, the same model
and settings throughout. A run counts as a hit when the expected skill is
loaded before the first file edit.

Setup details
-------------
- 20 prompts from my own backlog, rewritten to remove skill names.
- Each configuration was run twice on the full set.
- I logged tool calls from the session transcript, not from the model's reply.

Standard set results
--------------------
| Configuration                          | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|----------------------------------------|-------|-------|
| No hook                                | 50%   | 45%   |
| One-line reminder in the prompt hook   | 55%   | 50%   |
| Forced evaluation (YES/NO per skill)   | 100%  | 100%  |

The forced evaluation hook asks the model to write one YES/NO line per skill
before it starts working. It is noisy: every reply begins with a block of
evaluation lines, and users notice.

Notes on cost
-------------
Forced evaluation added roughly 150 output tokens per turn in my setup. The
reminder variant added nothing measurable. I did not measure latency.

A variant I almost left out
---------------------------
Before settling on forced evaluation I tried a different shape: a separate,
cheap classifier call runs outside the agent, reads the prompt and the skill
list, and injects the names of the relevant skills into the context. The agent
itself never writes an evaluation in its reply. On the standard set this
classifier variant also reached 100% in both runs.

I also tried the client's native prompt-type hook with exactly the same
instruction text as the forced evaluation. It scored 50%, no better than no
hook at all.

Hard set
--------
To separate the top two, I wrote 20 harder prompts where the right skill is
less obvious and some prompts need no skill at all.

| Configuration       | Correct | False positives |
|---------------------|---------|-----------------|
| Forced evaluation   | 15/20   | 0               |
| Classifier variant  | 13/20   | 3               |

What I use now
--------------
I kept forced evaluation because it had no false positives on the hard set,
even though the visible lines annoy me. If the classifier's false positives
can be fixed, I would switch, because it keeps replies clean.

# pagebrief

pagebrief fetches web pages for a research question and filters their text
with embedding similarity (threshold 0.35) before sending it to the model.
files.pagebrief/filters/keyword.py:
CHUNK_CHARS = 800


class KeywordFilter:
    """BM25-style ranking: keep chunks scoring at least a fraction of the best one."""

    def __init__(self, relative_threshold, max_chunks):
        self.relative_threshold = relative_threshold
        self.max_chunks = max_chunks

    def top(self, query, pages):
        chunks = [page["text"][i:i + CHUNK_CHARS] for page in pages
                  for i in range(0, len(page["text"]), CHUNK_CHARS)]
        words = set(query.lower().split())
        scored = [(sum(chunk.lower().count(w) for w in words), chunk) for chunk in chunks]
        best = max((score for score, _ in scored), default=0)
        kept = [chunk for score, chunk in sorted(scored, reverse=True)
                if best and score >= best * self.relative_threshold]
        return "\n\n".join(kept[:self.max_chunks])
